title: You know what? I am so angry about School Shooter Day.
body: Only fucking America. For those who are confused about the Tik Tok trend, basically it was a nationwide blanket threat that people were going to shoot up public schools, and then some towns or schools got more direct threats. So my school did not get a "direct threat" (which mind you was a term every student in America automatically made up and just knew what is was yesterday) but we were still under the general threat. However, in my state I know of three towns in my region that got direct threats. I go to a regional tech school btw. But I am so fucking angry that we had to, as a nation, be scared. I'm angry that my friends and I were debating on the bus which classes were the best and worst to escape from or be in during a lockdown. I'm angry that yesterday 1/3 of my school was gone because they didn't feel safe. I'm angry that I checked my phone every 10 minutes to look up the news, to check for threats, to update my friends and classmates. I'm angry that I was anxious sitting at my usually seat in the cafeteria with my back to the large window for fear of someone walking up and killing me. I'm angry that on the bus ride home I had to text my mom "I'm alive." So don't you dare make fun of my generation for taking a TikTok threat seriously, because the threat is there Every. Fucking. Day. yesterday it just got a little bit more real. Call me overdramatic if you want but this shit is real and I'm so fucking tired of being afraid at school.

title: Are GenZ being taught to desensitize to gun violence?
body:
Sorry about the formatting this is my first time posting!

I came across a TikTok where a man was talking about how the protocol for active shootings in schools and at work was odd.  He then brought up the question “are we being taught to desensitize to gun-related violence?” 

I thought about what he said and compared it to my own experience. 
In school, drills weren’t taken seriously. My teachers at the time would cover the window on our class door and tell us to continue working. When I did experience a school shooting nothing changed. The teacher told us “we're safe in here (classroom) so continue your work”. 
Throughout my entire high school experience, countless times intruders came into my school some with guns. I even experience a bomb threat and I didn't find out until I walk to school and a teacher confused me for a senior and told me that they were telling the lower grades that classes were being remodeled as to not scare them. When I asked her what I should do, she said “go home it will be fine.” 

Despite this, I'm still cautious around guns and take these events seriously. 

On the other hand, every time I turn on the news I expect to hear at least 5 times a week that a school is in lockdown because of an active shooter. 
I feel guilty but I usually just change the channel because at the moment I'm thinking “well I can't do anything about it right now.” 

I don't know where to go from here. Maybe talking it out or reading what you all think will help me come to an answer.

What do y'all think? 
Are we desensitized? 
What's your protocol for active shooters either at school or work?
Are the teachers just trying to keep us from being scared?

title: I went to school even when there was a threat
body:
I put this as nsfw for those little guys out there, this doesn’t have anything too bad in it, it’s just a serious topic that may not be appropriate for younger users.

I just remembered how fucked up this was. Back in December, on the last day of school before winter break there was a threat made against our school(making it vague so y’all can’t dox me sorry). I went to school anyway. Why? I don’t fucking know. It seemed that everyone knew about it and still went to school anyway and nobody seemed to care. It was like it was some sort of joke but there was no real evidence of it being one. It was so messed up that nobody even gave a shit until some parents found out. Later in the day around 10:00 my parents found out and they told me and my brother to leave class. When I left, I saw some confused faces as to why I was leaving and one of my friends said to me as I was checking out at the front desk, “Are you leaving? Where are you going? Damn, your parents kinda crazy too, huh? Mine are picking me up in like 30 minutes. Aight, see you.” He said that *his parents were crazy* for making him leave school when there was a literal threat against our school. Here’s an article about some of it, [right here](https://patch.com/virginia/fallschurch/tiktok-school-gun-threat-has-va-schools-law-enforcement-alert) I guess they had some reason to not cancel entirely because of this “trend” but they should have at least put out a warning. 


TLDR: There was a threat against my school and nobody gave a shit. :/
